summary: Introduces the Internet Engineering and Planning Group (IEPG) to the wider Internet community. The IEPG was a forum for engineers from network providers to coordinate operational matters. This is an informational introduction.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC introduces the Internet Engineering and Planning Group, a forum for Internet service operators. It describes the group's operational goals, open membership, and public meeting and document materials.

questions: who coordinated internet operations in the 1990s
who can join the iepg mailing list
subtitle: The charter and open membership of an Internet service-operator forum.

tldr.problem: Internet service operators needed a forum to coordinate operational aspects of managing Internet services.
tldr.mechanism: The IEPG brings operators together to facilitate operations and management, promote new services, and liaise with operational and technical groups.
tldr.outcome: The RFC introduces the group's charter, open membership, mailing list, and public archive; the IEPG does not conduct technical development.

today: RFC 1690 is Informational and describes the IEPG's charter as an open forum for coordinating Internet service operations. It does not specify a standard.

sections.title: Goal and Activities
sections.content:
The Internet Engineering and Planning Group (IEPG) is principally made up of Internet Service Operators. Its shared goal is to promote a technically coordinated operational environment for the global Internet.

Its activities include facilitating service operations and management, promoting new Internet services, and liaising with other operations and technical-development groups. The IEPG is explicitly not a technical-development group.
sections.plainLanguage: The IEPG focuses on coordinating operations and managing Internet services. It also connects operators with other operations and technical groups.

sections.title: Open Membership and Reporting
sections.content:
Membership is open to any individual who joins the mailing list. The RFC says meeting announcements, agendas, meetings, and reports are to be openly available.

The IEPG maintains an archive of its material using World Wide Web access tools. The RFC gives the mailing-list and archive addresses.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone may join the mailing list, and meeting information is public. The group also keeps an online archive of its material.

sections.title: Status of the Introduction
sections.content: RFC 1690 is an informational introduction to the IEPG and its charter. It does not specify an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC introduces an operator forum. It does not define a technical standard.
